narrative.coaching_note: The one change to make next time is to clean your hands at 11 seconds after you touched bed rail A and before you touched phone, using alcohol rub for 20 seconds or soap and water for 40 seconds. You picked up MRSA from bed rail A at 1.6 seconds, which created a Moment 5 opportunity you missed at 11 seconds. You then touched phone at 12.4 seconds and resident A at 21.4 seconds without any hand hygiene, which was also a Moment 1 opportunity before touching resident A at 21.4 seconds. That is how contamination reached resident A and why resident A was exposed at 21.4 seconds. Cleaning your hands at 11 seconds would have kept bare hand, gloved hand, phone, and resident A clean.
narrative.audit_summary: Staged clip with MRSA source bed rail A. Bare hand contacted bed rail A at 1.6 seconds, acquiring contamination, then transferred to call button at 7.6 seconds, phone at 12.4 seconds, and resident A at 21.4 seconds (chain length 4). Resident A exposure occurred at 21.4 seconds via bare hand. Hand hygiene compliance: overall 0/2, Moment 1 0/1, Moment 5 0/1; no hygiene events performed, so no agent efficacy or duration to assess. Alcohol rub is effective against MRSA per record. No glove use issues were recorded. Missed Moment 5 at 11 seconds after patient zone contact and missed Moment 1 at 21.4 seconds before resident contact. Surfaces requiring disinfection: bed rail A (source), call button, phone, and resident A contact area; use an EPA List H registered disinfectant effective against MRSA.
narrative.top_fix: The highest-impact single change in this clip was performing hand hygiene for Moment 5 at 11 seconds.
